newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish advertisers to increase agency spend in '97.
newsitem.headline: Danish advertisers to increase agency spend in '97.

text.p: Danish businesses think communication with consumers has become harder and many plan to raise overall advertising budgets and spend a larger proportion with agencies in 1997, a new survey says.

A poll of over 2,000 companies by the Danish Adversting Agency Industry Association published in the daily Berlingske Tidende on Wednesday showed that 92 percent of the surveyed expected to increase or maintain present advertising budgets and 20 percent would give their agencies more work.
"Our survey shows that recent years' growth will continue", the paper quotes association head Finn Kern as saying.
"We are happy about the survey's results and businesses' positive assessment of bureaux' contributions," he added.
He expected the optimism to lead to increased work force in the industry but added that caveat that increased agency billings were not always reflected in the bottom line.
"Earnings do not follow increasing turnovers due to hard competition and the fact that clients have become more price conscious when choosing advertising agencies", Kern said.
